lessons.title: കറുപ്പ്, വെള്ള, ചുവപ്പ്, നീല — the same split as Tamil
lessons.gloss: black, white, red, blue — Malayalam shares Tamil's native colors, and its Sanskrit blue too

segments.text: You've seen Malayalam and Tamil share day-names almost word-for-word. Their colors follow the exact same family pattern.
കറുപ്പ് (karuppŭ) = "black" — matches Tamil karuppu almost exactly.
വെള്ള (veḷḷa) = "white" — the same veḷ- "bright/silvery" root as Tamil veḷḷai.

ചുവപ്പ് (cuvappŭ) = "red" — a related word from the same Dravidian root family as Tamil sivappu, though the two differ in both their opening consonant's sound and their vowel — a looser cousin than karuppŭ/karuppu or veḷḷa/veḷḷai, which match almost exactly.

നീല (nīla) = "blue" — the same Sanskrit loan Tamil uses (nīlam), and the same one Hindi uses (nīlā). Blue is where Malayalam, Tamil, and Hindi all converge on one shared Sanskrit word, even though Malayalam and Tamil otherwise built their own native words for black, white, and red.

segments.source: [YOU SAY: "karuppŭ, veḷḷa, cuvappŭ" — black, white, red]

segments.instruction: "nīla" — blue, shared with Tamil and Hindi

segments.text: Which three Malayalam colors closely match Tamil's own words? (Karuppŭ, veḷḷa, cuvappŭ — black, white, red.) Which color is a shared Sanskrit loan across Malayalam, Tamil, and Hindi? (Blue — நீല nīla / நீலம் nīlam / नीला nīlā.)
